candidates.title: Commute Or Else
candidates.pitch: Each day deals a rack of seven operator tiles (add chips, add mult, multiply mult, echo the previous two tiles, mirror a neighbour, raise mult to a power) plus one immovable bedrock tile, and you slide them into the order that scores highest. A live score tree shows chips and mult after every tile, then a histogram of all 5,040 possible orderings reveals where your arrangement sits in a wildly long-tailed distribution, and an exact solver tells you the par. The delight is the first time you see one swap turn 400 into 4,000, and the palindrome rule that rewards symmetric racks.
candidates.whyNow: Timeless: ordering effects in chips-times-mult scoring are a perennial talking point among deckbuilder players, and a daily seeded puzzle with a shareable result grid keeps the page worth revisiting.

research.summary: Community guides on deckbuilder joker order agree on the shape of the maths: effects resolve left to right, flat mult belongs before multiplicative mult, and copy effects care about position (one copies its right neighbour, another copies the leftmost slot). That is exactly a non-commutative algebra, (c+a)*b differs from c*b+a, which I derived myself and will self-check in node. The number of orderings of eight items is 8! = 40320 per several counting references, so a rack of 7 movable tiles plus one fixed tile (5,040 orderings) is small enough for exact enumeration in a worker in milliseconds and big enough to have a fat-tailed score distribution worth drawing. Several community claims (exact examples, edge cases for scoring-triggered effects) were contradicted by one forum user, so the page uses its own stated rules, invented tile names and does not claim to reproduce any commercial game.

facts.claim: There are 8! = 40320 ways to order eight distinct items, so 7 movable tiles around one fixed tile give 7! = 5040 orderings (reference, as of 2026-10-12).
Community guides recommend flat mult sources left of multiplicative mult sources because jokers resolve left to right. Page text will say: as of 2026-10-12, per community guides, unconfirmed.
One forum user reported different behaviour for scoring-triggered effects, so edge cases are disputed in the community (unverified).
Position-based copy effects exist in the inspiration game (one reads its right neighbour, one reads the leftmost slot); reported by guides, unverified.

inspirations: histogram of all outcomes as in solver reports

design.coreLoop: Read today's rack and target, drag or keyboard-move tiles into slots, watch the score tree update tile by tile, submit, then see your rank among all 5,040 orderings and the solver's par. The second minute is learning that add-before-multiply is not always best (echo and mirror tiles and the exponent tile bend it); the tenth is hunting palindromic racks and chasing par with fewer moves. A seeded daily rack plus unlimited practice racks by hash keeps it fresh.
sophisticationHooks: Exact enumeration of all orderings in a worker with a histogram showing where the player's order lands (percentile, par, worst)
Score tree waterfall that shows chips and mult after each tile, with a reverse-the-rack toggle to show non-commutativity
Tile set with echo (repeat previous two tiles, the riff), mirror (copy right neighbour), exponent, bedrock (fixed slot) and a palindrome symmetry bonus
Seeded generator guarantees a unique optimum, and a node self-check validates the evaluator against hand-computed racks
design.scopeForOneDay: Built: tile evaluator and enumerator (pure functions), seeded rack generator, drag and keyboard slotting, score tree SVG, histogram, share string and URL hash, about panel, light and dark, reduced motion. Cut: accounts, leaderboards, animations beyond tile slide, sound.
risks: Resemblance to a past scoring-engine toy: tags avoid joker and mod vocabulary and the loop is a puzzle, not a sandbox
Community rule claims are unverified, so the page uses its own invented tile names and states its rules rather than claiming to reproduce any game
Unique-optimum racks need generator care; fall back to showing ties
Floating point: keep scores as integers under 2^53 by capping the exponent tile

candidates.title: Synergy Overflow
candidates.pitch: You are the founder of an invented company pitching buzzword cards to a very gullible board: some add headcount, some add hype, some multiply it by synergy, and a few raise it to a power called disruption. Targets grow like an idle game's cost curve, order matters, and by quarter twenty the numbers have names nobody learned, until the page finally overflows into a deliberate, theatrical NaN-e-Inf board meeting. The joke is the deadpan corporate voice, the payoff is watching the maths run out of numbers.
candidates.whyNow: Timeless satire of numbers-go-up design and corporate buzzword inflation; it also fills the owed humor slot with a real mechanic rather than a one-liner.

research.summary: Incremental and idle games rest on a simple recipe: costs rise exponentially (a growth factor of 1.15 per purchase is the convention popularised by one famous clicker, per an analysis paper and a developer write-up) while income rises more slowly, so designers tune payback time and reset with prestige. The deckbuilder community has a famous joke ending: scores that exceed double precision display as a garbled overflow word, with an endless-mode wall and mods that push the cap far higher. That pairing, exponential targets plus an overflow punchline, is a real mechanic with a built-in comedic ending. The satire targets generic corporate speak with an invented company; no real firms or people.

sources.snippet: Write-up of a live speedrun event run that reached the naneinf overflow state in a bit over an hour, naming the word as NaN plus e plus Inf.
sources.note: The overflow joke is real and celebrated in the community.

sources.note: Independent site agreeing that a naneinf overflow state exists.

sources.note: Third site mentioning the cap and that mods extend it.

facts.claim: A cost growth factor of 1.15 per purchase is a common idle-game convention, cited for one famous clicker (as of 2026-10-12).
In the inspiration game, scores beyond the floating-point limit show as an overflow state nicknamed naneinf, discussed by an event write-up, a forum thread and a mod description (as of 2026-10-12).

The double-precision limit is about 1.8 times 10 to the 308; one forum estimate puts the overflow near that figure. The page will compute this itself in the browser and label the forum figure as reported.
A 2026 live event write-up reports a player reaching the overflow state in a run of about 1 hour 16 minutes (reported by one source, unverified).

inspirations: the overflow joke ending of deckbuilder endless modes

design.coreLoop: Each quarter the board sets a target; you draw five buzzword cards, play up to four in an order you choose, and the score tree runs in front of you with a deadpan commentary line per card. Beat the target to get a perk card for the deck or restructure (prestige) to reset with a permanent multiplier. It stays interesting because order, exponent cards and a rising deck-thinning decision make each draw a small optimisation, and because the ending is a joke worth reaching.
sophisticationHooks: Log-space big-number type (mantissa plus exponent) with named-number formatting beyond the 15-digit double limit
Target curve built from a tunable growth factor and payback-time check so a run lasts about 25 quarters
Optional chief-of-staff hint that brute-forces card orders and shows the best order score without revealing the card choice
Scripted overflow finale: the display glitches into NaN-e-Inf, the board applauds, and the run ends with a shareable certificate
design.scopeForOneDay: Built: card pool of about 30 invented buzzword cards, run loop with seeded draws, big-number class with tests, commentary lines, overflow finale, share string, about panel, light and dark, reduced motion. Cut: sound, meta-progression beyond one prestige layer, more than one company.
risks: Humor must land: commentary lines need a writing pass and generic invented company names only, no real firms, brands or people
Looks like an idle toy; mitigate with decisions every turn and a defined ending
Overlap with the carried-over Breaking Changes humor idea is thematic only (corporate voice), so the mechanic and subject are different
Floating-point claims: the page states the double limit as computed in-browser and labels forum figures as reported
Event write-up detail (run time) is from one result and stays unverified
